name: ACAN
summary: ACAN, a dwarfism locus with five alleles. A horse is affected when it has no working copy left, so two different variant alleles together still count. One pairing (D1/D1) is lethal at birth; every other affected combination is a surviving dwarf with reduced health. No wild horse is ever born affected - only two carriers bred together.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies of ACAN. Normal skeletal growth.

phenotypes.name: ACAN carrier
phenotypes.description: One broken copy and one working one. The horse is a normal size and there is no way to see it. Two carriers bred together throw a dwarf one time in four - and it does not matter whether they carry the same variant.

phenotypes.name: Chondrodysplastic dwarfism
phenotypes.description: No working copy of ACAN. The horse is markedly small with shortened limbs, moves badly, jumps badly, and has far fewer hearts than it should.

phenotypes.name: Lethal dwarfism (D1/D1)
phenotypes.description: Two copies of the severe D1 variant. The foal is born profoundly malformed and does not survive.
